content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm facing an unusual issue with [article_no] and [product_name] [version_no]. My program includes several hour counters performing standard time tracking with default settings—no special options or preloads. When I attempt to read these counter values in [product_name], I see the correct names for my time counters, but the values for OT seem invalid. I've tried numerous adjustments, such as setting a preload value, but the numbers remain unchanged. Strangely, the outputs linked to these hour counters function as expected. Does anyone know why I’m seeing these unexpected 5000+ OT hours? See the attachment captured from [product_name].

Hi, 1. Try testing with just an OHC and message text. 2. If successful, the issue could be related to OHC FB numbers being above 200. How to modify FB-Number: 1. Locate a basic function, such as AND/OR, with an FB-Number less than 200. 2. Replace one using the same function (drag and drop from the instruction tree). 3. Add an OHC; it should then have a new FB-Number under 200. Repeat this process for the other five OHCs. Then reconnect and check if the new setup works. Hope this is helpful.

Yes, that makes sense. Using a simple block resolves the problem, and I suspect it’s the same reason I can’t create UDF blocks. Is there any official documentation covering these details, or is it just something users discover through experience? Also, is there an automated block renumbering feature in [product_name]? Ideally, though, this should be addressed in the firmware itself. I'm confident renumbering will fix the issue, but with more than 300 blocks, it's far from straightforward and could cause regression problems. Thanks for the prompt advice; it definitely saved me some trouble. Kind regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user observed that hour counter values in [product_name] [version_no] are displayed incorrectly when working with a large program exceeding 200 function blocks, despite outputs functioning normally. There was also frustration over limited documentation and lack of features to manage complex and extensive projects, particularly automated block renumbering.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects hour counter values in [product_name] to be reliable for any number of function blocks, regardless of program complexity. They also expect comprehensive documentation and practical tools to simplify large project management.
